title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel / disconnect / reconnect / server timeouts
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: streaming endpoints have become a frequent source of customer-facing instability: abrupt client cancels leave in-progress model state (KV caches, batching slots) held indefinitely, and transient disconnects break UX continuity. This PR implements end-to-end lifecycle controls to make streaming robust across client-initiated cancel, ungraceful disconnects, and reconnect/resume flows while adding server-side timeouts and sane fallback behavior.

What changed (high level):
- Introduces a streaming session abstraction (SessionID + ephemeral metadata) that can be attached to streaming responses to enable safe resume semantics.
- Client cancel handling: explicit CANCEL control messages (and OpenAI-compatibility: streaming "[DONE]" semantics preserved) cause an immediate service-side stop, early KV cache release, and metrics tagging (canceled=true).
- Disconnect handling: on TCP/HTTP/WS disconnect, server marks session as disconnected and keeps ephemeral state for a configurable grace window (default 30s) to allow reconnect/resume. After grace window expiry server performs cleanup.
- Reconnect/resume: clients may reconnect with SessionID within the grace window to resume streaming; resume is best-effort and validates prefix/KV compatibility. When incompatible, server falls back to a non-resume completion (single final message) and logs the reason.
- Server-side idle/timeouts: adds two timeout tiers (inflight idle timeout and disconnected TTL) with runtime-config flags and per-customer overrides in Dedicated/Private.
- OpenAI compatibility layer updates: SSE event format clarified, resume control events documented, and function/tool-calling event ordering preserved across reconnects.
- Tests: new unit/e2e tests cover cancel, disconnect, reconnect success/failure, and tool-calling across resumes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Session abstraction and store (in-memory + optional redis-backed pluggable store)
- [x] Cancel control path and metrics tagging
- [x] Disconnect detection and grace window with scheduled cleanup job
- [x] Reconnect validation and resume logic with compatibility checks
- [x] OpenAI-compat SSE/event changes + backward-compatible fallbacks
- [x] Unit and e2e tests
- [x] Documentation updates in redwood-docs (streaming/resume docs)

Breaking changes: none by default; OpenAI-compat SSE adds new optional resume events but continues to accept legacy clients. Operators can opt into stricter resume validation via feature flags.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the default grace window conservative (30s) to avoid excessive memory retention; ops can increase for low-traffic Dedicated customers. Further follow-ups (ENG-9473) will add mem-sensitive eviction heuristics and telemetry sampling for resumed sessions.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain why the default grace window is 30s? Curious about memory retention in heavy load.
Maya Patel: 30s is conservative to balance UX and memory; we expose tunables per-customer and will add eviction heuristics in follow-up ENG-9473.
Sofia Alvarez: For OpenAI-compat, will legacy clients break if we send resume events?
Maya Patel: No — resume events are optional and are sent as separate SSE control events; legacy clients will ignore unknown events. We also keep the final [DONE] event for backward compatibility.
Devon Brooks: e2e flake on CI where reconnect timing slightly overshoots the grace window on slow runners — can we make test tolerant?
Maya Patel: Increased tolerance in tests and added retry loop for the test harness to reduce flakes. Also added a CI gate to rerun flaky e2e once automatically.
Liam Chen: Approve after addressing small nit re: metric labels.
Maya Patel: Metrics label change applied (streaming_session_state -> streaming_session_phase).

release_notes: Improved streaming reliability: client-initiated cancel now releases resources immediately, transient disconnects are tolerated with a 30s default grace window for reconnect/resume, and server-side timeouts + OpenAI-compatible resume events added. Operators can tune grace window and idle timeouts per deployment.
